title: Session-window pricing prototype for asymmetric input/output and streaming prorates
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Run a lightweight experiment that evaluates charging by per-session windows instead of strict per-request IO accounting to smooth billing for streaming-heavy customers. We will measure whether a session-window approach (aggregate tokens across a session and apply asymmetric input/output rates with a streaming prorate) reduces customer surprise and improves revenue predictability without materially changing unit economics. This prototype focuses on hosted API customers using streaming and long-lived chat sessions (>=60s).
hypothesis: H1: Applying an input/output asymmetric multiplier at session level (IO_ratio) with a streaming prorate for partial-stream sessions will reduce billing variance for chat workloads by >=30%.
H2: Net revenue per active user will change by <5% when using session-window pricing versus current per-call metering for customers with median session lengths between 10s and 6 minutes.
H3: Customer support ticket volume about 'surprise bills' will decrease for experiment cohort versus control.
experiment_design: Cohort assignment: 5% of new hosted-api customers (opt-out via billing flag) assigned to session-window pricing for 60 days.
Session definition: contiguous websocket/HTTP streaming connection with <120s idle gap counts as single session; all tokens within session aggregated for billing window.
Rates: input_token_rate = $0.000010/token, output_token_rate = $0.000018/token by default for session cohort (asymmetric IO ratio = 1.8).
Streaming prorate: if session ends mid-stream due to disconnect, bill prorated streaming discount: streaming_prorate = min(1.0, active_stream_time / 30s).
Minimums: apply per-session floor of 5 tokens equivalent billed per session to reduce tiny-call noise; enterprise customers can opt-in to session minima waiver.
Fallback: requests flagged for special handling (tests, evals, embeddings) are excluded and billed at existing per-call metering.
Instrumentation: emit telemetry events billing.session.start, billing.session.end, billing.session.tokens.{input,output}, billing.session.adjusted_charge.
metrics: Primary: Billing variance per customer (stddev of daily bill over 14 day windows)
Secondary: revenue delta vs control cohort, average charge per session, support tickets referencing 'billing' or 'surprise', API latency percentiles (to ensure no perf impact)
Safety: percent of sessions that trigger edge cases (idle gaps > 120s, aborted streams, very large sessions > 50k tokens)
acceptance_criteria: A1: Billing variance reduced >= 20% compared to control for chat-heavy customers
A2: Revenue per MAU delta within +/-5% vs control over the 30-day rolling window
A3: No increase in API 95th latency beyond historical baseline +5%
A4: No more than 3% of sessions hit billing edge-case handling without automated reconciliation

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers on bursty patterns could see lower or higher bills unexpectedly. Mitigation: opt-out via billing flag + targeted comms to top 50 customers before ramp.
Risk: Billing pipeline complexity introduces reconciliation bugs. Mitigation: run parallel simulator + reconciliation job and hold invoices in draft state for cohort for 48 hours.
Risk: Enterprise contracts require explicit invoice line items. Mitigation: work with Legal to create invoice template and record mapping for SQ responses.
early_findings: Day 7 interim: Telemetry shows 92% of sessions are < 3 minutes; streaming prorate mostly 1.0 (full credit) for sessions >30s.
Charge distribution: small call noise reduced by 37% due to per-session floor aggregation. Support tickets referencing 'weird microcharges' decreased in test cohort (sampled) compared to control.
Edge case: ~1.1% of sessions aborted mid-stream due to mobile network disconnects; current prorate formula bills at 0.6x for these—identifying potential unfairness for long partial streams.
